Rule and exact checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:

Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Finding rationale:
Section 2.1 is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT: a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights", so it fails the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up) and there is no convenience exit elsewhere. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We therefore take the preferred position: § 2.1 is replaced with an express no-minimum-commitment statement, and § 7.1 already limits us to the Fees stated in each Order Form (usage-based where so priced) and bars unidentified minimum-use charges, so we pay only for usage or ordered Services.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
p0025: 7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.
p0044: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Order Form: 1.6 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered operative language:
2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment.
7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.
12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced § 2.1 with an express statement that we have no minimum purchase or volume commitment, consistent with Vendor's acknowledgement in § 12.3 and with § 7.1 (we pay only Order Form Fees and no unidentified minimum-use charges). If a commitment is essential, we could discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ..." — the obligations in (a)-(c) are triggered by every expiry and every termination, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months" — matches the six-month ceiling; the request condition tracks the model language and is not tied to expiry only.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) ends "at Vendor's then-current rates."

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data" — the clock is anchored to the termination/expiry event, not to a Customer request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format."

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion to Customer in writing" — deletion is expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason."

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six months of assistance in limb (a) exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days after the expiry or termination.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 10.1 references an "agreed transition period" without creating one, Section 10.2 addresses only Deliverables and refunds, and Section 16.5 expressly routes Customer Data away to Sections 11 and 15, which contain no export, return, or deletion-timing mechanic.
All six preferred elements are met in operative language, so the redline is position-complete at the preferred level (and a fortiori at the fallback).

Minimality holds: the proposal is a single concise insertion in the termination section with no deletions or paraphrase of surrounding text; it adds no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, cost allocation, or procedure beyond the checklist. Extending the trigger to "or any Order Form" is justified by the document's Order Form structure and Section 10.1's reference to "terminated subscription Services" (partial termination), so it is not surplus.

Intent is preserved: refund and Deliverables mechanics in 10.2, the access wind-down in 10.1, and the confidentiality return/destroy regime in 16.5 all survive without contradiction; the new clause supplies the substantive Customer Data exit mechanic that was absent.

Two housekeeping points for the drafter (not defects in the checklist): (i) the rendered insertion carries no section number although the rationale calls it Section 10.3 — number it so cross-references remain clean; (ii) Section 16.5's retained sentence "Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15" could be read as excluding the new Section 10 mechanic, and Section 11 is empty, so consider siting the clause in Section 15 or conforming the Section 16.5 cross-reference rather than adding a broad notwithstanding override.

elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Revised § 2.1 reads: "Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment." This replaces the prior USD 2,000,000/year three-year take-or-pay obligation and is consistent with § 12.3 ("Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment").

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained § 7.1: "Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form ... unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify." Fees are defined as amounts payable under an Order Form, so payment is limited to ordered Services or usage-priced items.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no commitment survives after § 2.1 is replaced with an express no-minimum-commitment statement, so there is nothing to limit to a 12-month term. The fallback checklist is moot because the preferred (stronger) outcome is achieved.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment remaining in § 2.1, there is no commitment requiring a reduction right. The margin comment offers this fallback only if Vendor insists on a commitment.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no shortfall mechanic, take-or-pay formula, or penalty remains anywhere in the cited language after § 2.1 is replaced; § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: § 2.1 as rendered is an unconditional statement that Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment, and retained § 7.1 confines payment to Fees stated in each Order Form (usage-priced where the Order Form so provides) while barring unidentified minimum-use charges.

Minimal: only § 2.1 was rewritten, and the replacement is a concise substitute for the offending take-or-pay sentence. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or extra requirements were added; §§ 7.1 and 12.3 are retained verbatim and no Customer-favourable wording elsewhere was deleted.

Preserves intent: the Fees, Order Form, and Services definitions and the payment mechanics in § 7.1 continue to operate; removing the take-or-pay obligation leaves no dangling cross-reference, undefined trigger, or contradictory retained sentence, and it resolves the prior conflict with § 12.3's acknowledgement of no minimum-volume commitment.
No residual shortfall, instalment, or contingent payment formula remains, so the deletion is unconditional rather than merely narrowed.

Fallback elements are recorded as met only because their condition (an existing commitment) no longer applies; if Vendor insists on reinstating a commitment, the drafter must then add the 12-month limit, the 30-day reduction right, and an express true-up in operative text rather than in the margin comment.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-91fc55b3","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","rationale":"There is no indemnification clause anywhere in the Agreement: the numbering jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and searches for \"indemnify\", \"hold harmless\", \"defend\", and infringement remedies return no operative grant. Sections 9.3 (\"remedies required by Section 20.5\"), 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 29.2, and 30.5 all presuppose indemnification obligations and indemnified parties that the document never creates, so Customer has no Vendor IP or misconduct indemnity — walk-away territory. We insert a new Section 20.1 at the preferred level (Vendor defence/indemnity for Services and Deliverables IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with notice, control of defence, and cooperation) and cap any Customer indemnity at Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. We deliberately did not take the fallback: its 3× annual fees super-cap would be worse for us than Section 21.3, which already treats indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims.","proposal":"Insert missing Section 20 Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation procedure and a narrow Customer indemnity limit.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-9ffc113c","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for (and paid for by) Customer and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails even the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables. The rest of the IP architecture already sits at our preferred position: Customer owns Customer Data with Vendor's rights limited to processing it to provide, secure, support and improve the Services (14.1); Vendor retains Vendor Technology, defined as its pre-existing technology (14.3, 1.8); Customer has a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable (13.2, 14.3); and no joint ownership arises absent a signed instrument setting out exploitation rights (14.4). The shortest complete cure is therefore to reverse 14.2 to Customer ownership with an express assignment, which leaves 13.2, 14.3 and 10.1 intact.","proposal":"Customer owns Deliverables; Vendor assigns them","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-ff4e9714","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"The clause meets the preferred position in full. § 21.1 imposes an expressly mutual aggregate cap at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. § 21.2 excludes indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive and consequential damages mutually (\"neither Party\"), and helpfully confirms that Customer Data restoration, replacement services, notice and incident-response costs are direct damages. § 21.3 places outside the cap each Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment obligation is not damages subject to the Section. \"Fees\" (§ 1.5) is a substantive recurring subscription/professional services/usage fee base, so the cap is not illusory; § 21.4 preserves each cap independently and prevents the exclusions from swallowing unlawfully limited liability. Two immaterial points noted only for the record: Fees exclude a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form says otherwise, and the payment carve-out is confined to \"undisputed Fees for conforming Services\" (a narrowing in our favour). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-f67decf2","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets our preferred position. 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without Vendor's consent (notice only), and 13.3 carries our licence rights across such a transfer. 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, so there is no walk-away trigger. Two points are noted only, not redlined: the competitor bar is framed as subject to our consent rather than absolute, and 24.3's mutual consent requirement for other assignments applies symmetrically, which does not disadvantage us given the broad 24.1 carve-out.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-5af4c6fe","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"Section 12.3 (p0044) expressly preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, and records that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. No clause anywhere imposes a sole-supplier, all-requirements, or no-third-party-procurement obligation on us, so the rule sits at the preferred position. Section 7.2 (p0026) is a disclose-and-match / most-favoured-offer mechanic and does not prohibit engaging another provider once honoured, so it is handled under MFN, not exclusivity. Section 2.1 (p0012) is a take-or-pay minimum-volume commitment (and Section 12.4's competing-product covenant a non-compete); those are minimum-commitment and restrictive-covenant issues for their own rules and are not sourcing exclusivity, so we do not flag them twice here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-76ab2172","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 27.3 If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee on Customer anywhere, so it sits at our preferred position (\"Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties\"). Termination provisions (§§9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2) contain no exit fee or acceleration of remaining term value, and §27.3 expressly allows Customer to terminate \"without penalty\" with a refund of prepaid Fees. §7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due, and §22.2 shifts only reasonable audit costs plus the undisputed shortfall on a >5% underpayment, which is actual cost/amount recovery rather than a stipulated penalty. The §2.1 take-or-pay minimum is a volume commitment reviewed under the minimum-commitment rule and is not double-flagged here. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-7bed9df8","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"The licence package meets our preferred position in full. § 13.1 grants the subscription right to \"Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf\"; § 13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a \"perpetual, irrevocable\" fully paid licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology (extended to Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables by § 14.3); and § 13.3 limits Vendor revocation or suspension to a material uncured breach after notice and a cure opportunity, and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by § 24 (which allows Customer assignment to a merger/acquisition successor without Vendor consent). Affiliate coverage is automatic in the grant, so no written-notice mechanic is needed. Noted, not flagged here: the revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in § 14.2 conflicts with this package; that is a Deliverable ownership/licence issue addressed under the IP rule and we do not double-flag it.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-00a4a55e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"Section 12.4 binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete (\"any product or service that competes with Vendor\"), covering development, marketing, sale and acquisition, in any territory, for the term plus 24 months. That is walk-away territory on two counts: a post-term restraint longer than 12 months and undefined scope; it also fails every fallback element (no named product, post-term application, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out). It further contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer \"has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.\" We therefore reverse the prohibition to the preferred position so Customer carries no non-compete or field-of-use restriction, leaving Section 12.3 consistent.","proposal":"Remove the Customer non-compete in Section 12.4","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-b5a8fdcb","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","rationale":"Section 12.4 is the only non-solicitation provision in the document, and it fails the fallback on every material term: it binds Customer only (not mutual), covers any Vendor employee rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs for the term plus twenty-four months rather than 12 months after involvement ends, contains an express no-hire (\"hire, or employ\"), and rules out both a general-advertising and an unsolicited-approach carve-out (\"regardless of how the employee applies\"). A no-hire covering all Vendor personnel is walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment. We therefore target the preferred position and replace the restrictive words with confirmation that Customer takes no non-solicitation restriction, which also removes the internal conflict with 12.3. The separate Section 12.4 non-compete is a different commercial term and is not flagged here.","proposal":"Replace the one-sided 24-month no-hire/non-solicit in Section 12.4 with a confirmation that Customer takes no such restriction.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-e4434243","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"The three-year term (§ 8.1) contains no Customer termination-for-convenience right: Section 9 gives only for-cause, insolvency and security/SLA/legal-violation rights, and § 2.1 expressly commits Customer on a take-or-pay basis \"without reduction or termination rights\". Section 8.2 non-renewal is a natural-term right (RENEWAL) and § 27.3 is a force-majeure exit, so neither substitutes. Section 10.2's refund of \"prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination\" is not expressly pro rata and excludes prepaid non-recurring Fees, so it does not satisfy the refund element. We therefore add a new § 9.4 giving Customer a 30 days' notice convenience right with a pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period and barring Vendor convenience termination during a committed term, and conform § 2.1 while preserving the no-reduction restriction.","proposal":"Add a Customer 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, bar Vendor convenience termination, and conform the take-or-pay clause.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-audit-fd697e2e","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 is the only audit right binding us (Section 23 has a heading but no operative text, and no other inspection/verification right exists). It meets every preferred element: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, off-site where practicable, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1); Vendor bears costs unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly (22.2). Section 22.3 additionally makes findings our Confidential Information. No redline is warranted; this sits at the preferred position, above the fallback.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-4a18e833","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","rationale":"Section 28.1 imposes Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — Vendor-side territory outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and walk-away on its face. It also directly contradicts Section 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out (that carve-out does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum). The shortest complete cure is to change the governing law in 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore jurisdiction wording, leaving 28.2's venue intact so the clause sits at the preferred position.","proposal":"Change governing law in 28.1 from Singapore to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore exclusive jurisdiction wording.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-aa0c1dbb","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"The first Section 7.2 imposes an MFN-style obligation on us: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. That is open-ended — no defined product, no time limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory, and it contradicts Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. This is a disclose-and-match mechanic only and is not double-flagged as exclusivity. The redline replaces the obligation with an express confirmation that no disclose-or-match obligation applies, achieving the preferred position; Vendor-granted MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.","proposal":"Replace the Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation with an express statement that no such obligation applies.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-70be8bbe","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 2.1 is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT: a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\", so it fails the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up) and there is no convenience exit elsewhere. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We therefore take the preferred position: § 2.1 is replaced with an express no-minimum-commitment statement, and § 7.1 already limits us to the Fees stated in each Order Form (usage-based where so priced) and bars unidentified minimum-use charges, so we pay only for usage or ordered Services.","proposal":"Replace the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1 with an express no-minimum-commitment statement","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-33e30b33","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"Renewal terms sit at our preferred position. § 8.2 provides automatic successive twelve-month renewal terms (no multi-year renewals), a Customer non-renewal notice window of only thirty days, and a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal (with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which further favours us). § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of trailing twelve-month CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. Every preferred conditional automatic-renewal element is therefore satisfied, so mutual written agreement is not required and no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-de310d78","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","rationale":"This is a hosted services agreement, but nothing obliges Vendor to provide exit assistance or to return Customer Data. Section 10.1 only ends access \"after any agreed transition period\" (no agreed period exists and no assistance obligation is created), Section 10.2 covers Deliverables and refunds only, and Section 16.5's return-or-destroy duty for Confidential Information expressly defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, neither of which contains any export, return, or deletion-timing mechanic (Section 11 has no text; Section 15 addresses processing limits and privacy). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Eleven clauses sit at or above our preferred position and require no redline — notably the mutual liability cap and carve-outs (§ 21), the licence grant package (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), renewal mechanics (§ 8.2–8.3), Vendor's audit rights (§ 22), the performance warranty suite (§ 19) and insurance (§ 18).

Eight items need attention, and several are serious. Three are critical: the Agreement contains **no indemnification clause at all** (the numbering jumps from § 19 to § 21) even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 29.2 and 30.5 all presuppose one; § 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable we pay for, with only a revocable term-limited licence back; and there is no post-termination transition assistance or Customer Data return mechanic anywhere in a hosted-services deal.

A cluster of Customer-side restrictions is also unacceptable and, tellingly, internally inconsistent: § 12.4 imposes an undefined-scope non-compete and an all-personnel no-hire for the term plus 24 months, § 7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match MFN obligation, and § 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — all of which contradict § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Separately, § 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which conflicts with § 28.2's New York County exclusive venue, and there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right.

## 2. Findings

We insert a new § 20 at the preferred level (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control of defence and cooperation, plus a narrow Customer indemnity. We did not take the fallback: its 3× fees super-cap is worse than § 21.3, which already treats indemnification as an uncapped Excluded Claim. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; Customer gets a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails even the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify, sublicense). Cure: reverse to Customer ownership with express assignment. §§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.4, 13.2 already sit at preferred. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) | Preferred position met: mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion with restoration/incident costs confirmed as direct; robust uncapped Excluded Claims. No redline. |

| 6 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-sided, all-Vendor-employee no-hire for term plus 24 months, "regardless of how the employee applies" (no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out). Walk-away. Cure: replace with confirmation that Customer takes no such restriction. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 2.1 (with §§ 8.1, 9, 10.2) | Three-year term with no Customer convenience right; § 2.1 says "without reduction or termination rights". § 8.2 non-renewal and § 27.3 force majeure are not substitutes, and § 10.2's refund is not expressly pro rata. Cure: new § 9.4 — 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Preferred: notice-only Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors, Vendor assignment gated by our consent, competitor bar, and § 24.4 denies Vendor any repricing or termination on our change of control. No redline. |
| 9 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | Preferred: express freedom to develop, acquire, license or use any product and engage any supplier; no sole-supplier or all-requirements clause. §§ 7.2, 2.1 and 12.4 are handled under MFN, MINCOMMIT and NONCOMPETE and not double-flagged. |

| 11 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2, 13.3, 14.3) | Preferred: Affiliates and contractors covered in the grant; perpetual irrevocable licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology; revocation limited to uncured material breach; transferable on a permitted § 24 assignment. § 14.2 conflict addressed under IP. |

Walk-away, and contradicts § 12.3. Cure: replace with an express no-minimum-commitment statement (§ 7.1 already limits us to Order Form Fees). |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2, 22.3) | Preferred: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor-borne costs unless >5% underpayment, no direct system access, findings are our Confidential Information. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | Preferred: 12-month renewals, 30-day Customer opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | At or above preferred: professional/workmanlike and conformance warranties, 90-day Deliverable period plus full-term hosted conformance, law-compliance and no-malicious-code warranties, non-exclusive remedies, and § 19.5 prevents the disclaimer swallowing the warranty. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | Preferred limits met in full (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp, employer's liability), term plus one year, certificates on request. No redline. |

## 3. Walk-away items

The following must be resolved before signature. Each is identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory or as a failure of the fallback on a material term:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing § 20).** We have no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity, while six other sections assume one exists. Non-negotiable.
2. **§ 14.2 — Vendor ownership of Deliverables.** Fails even the fallback licence-back. We require Customer ownership with express assignment.
3. **§ 12.4 — non-compete (term + 24 months, undefined scope) and all-personnel no-hire (term + 24 months, no carve-outs).** Both walk-away; both contradict § 12.3.
4. **§ 2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights.** Walk-away; contradicts § 12.3 and is compounded by the absence of any convenience exit.
5. **§ 28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction.** Outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and inconsistent with § 28.2.
6. **§ 7.2 — open-ended disclose-and-match MFN.** Fails the fallback and approaches walk-away; contradicts § 12.3.
7. **No transition assistance or Customer Data return (missing from § 10).** Fails the fallback in a hosted-services deal where our data sits with Vendor.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviation and missing items: new § 20 (Vendor indemnity with notice/control/cooperation and a narrow Customer indemnity); § 14.2 reversed to Customer ownership with assignment; new § 10.3 (six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion); new § 9.4 (30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience termination during a committed term) with § 2.1 conformed; § 12.4 restrictions removed; § 7.2 MFN obligation replaced; § 2.1 replaced with a no-minimum-commitment statement; § 28.1 changed to New York law with the Singapore jurisdiction wording deleted.
2. **Lead with the internal inconsistencies.** §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3, and § 28.1 contradicts § 28.2. These are the cheapest wins and should be framed as conforming the document to Vendor's stated positions.
3. **Flag the drafting gap in § 20** to Vendor directly, noting the § 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 29.2 and 30.5 cross-references to obligations the document never creates; we expect Vendor to treat this as an error rather than a negotiation.
4. **Confirm with the business** the commercial appetite on § 2.1 volume and § 12.4 competing-product scope, so we know which fallbacks (if any) we are authorised to accept.
5. **Hold the compliant clauses.** §§ 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 8.2–8.3, 12.3 and 27.3 sit at or above our preferred position; we should resist any reopening of these as consideration for the changes above.
